observation.visible_scene: A single scoop of glossy white ice cream sits on top of a waffle cone, which rests in a shallow pool of white melted liquid on a light surface, all set against a near-black background. Faint orange-pink tones show through the cone's grid texture. The framing is tight on the cone, with the dark background filling the upper half of the image.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the scoop slowly deforms in place rather than translating: the pronounced crease/peak on its upper surface smooths out, the top rounds off, and the right-side edge bulges outward slightly, so the scoop's silhouette becomes lower and more domed.
The white coating on the cone thickens and runs downward, partially obscuring the waffle grid; the orange-tinted texture remains visible but shifts in appearance as the white flows over it.
The white pool at the base spreads marginally, its left rim extending a little and its surface shape subtly changing, consistent with ongoing melt accumulation.
The overall object stays at the same position in the frame; the visible changes are shape deformation and surface flow, not movement of the cone across the scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happened before t=0 (initial shape, temperature, any cause of melting) and what happens after the last frame (further collapse, full melt) are not shown.
Whether the white pool and the scoop are the same material or different substances is not determinable from the clip.
uncertain_details: A very small camera drift or reframing cannot be fully ruled out, but background and object positions look essentially fixed, so the dominant change is read as physical deformation of the ice cream.
The exact cause of the deformation (melting vs. settling) is inferred from appearance only; no heat source or contact is visible.
